notes: §1985:VII.2.12.3 SR5: "Only one RERUN clause containing the CLOCK-UNITS phrase may be specified." The clause is 1985-only: rerunClause parses it at every edition, VisitRerunClause refuses it from 2002 (COBOL0902), and at --std 85 BindIoControl collects the paragraph's RERUN clauses and ScreenRerunClauses asks the five syntax rules; the clause is otherwise a null rerun facility. ScreenRerunClauses walks every RERUN clause of the I-O-CONTROL paragraph with one flag for the CLOCK-UNITS arm of rerunEvery and reports COBOL6531 at each clause after the first that writes the phrase, whatever its ON operand or integer. Probed at --std 85 beyond the witness (two adjacent CLOCK-UNITS clauses with one implementor-name): two with different implementor-names are refused, and so is a second one separated from the first by a RECORDS clause and a SAME clause; one CLOCK-UNITS clause beside a RECORDS clause is accepted.

next.reason: 1985: "Only one RERUN clause containing the CLOCK-UNITS phrase may be specified."; 2023: "No candidate covers the RERUN clause or the CLOCK-UNITS phrase; the feature is absent from 2023.". No 2023 clause holds the RERUN feature, and no wording candidate addresses RERUN or CLOCK-UNITS. The 2023 standard lacks the RERUN clause, so the rule is dropped.
